text:
alex.h: Heads up — seeing a sharp TTFT spike (~200ms -> 700ms p95) on /v1/generate starting ~08:12 UTC. Decode time is flat but kernel_time attribution is low. Suspect kernel selection or kernel load latency + KV miss cascade.

maya: Can you paste the per-token breakdown from the dashboard? TTFT vs decode vs kernel_init?

alex.h: Quick paste from the token breakdown chart (abbreviated):
```
TTFT_p95: 700ms
decode_p95: 120ms
kernel_time_p95: 90ms
kernel_init_p95: 420ms
kvcache_miss_rate: 18% -> normally 2-3%
```

jordan: Hmm kernel_init being 420ms screams "kernel binary / cache miss" or new compilation path. Did we roll anything touching kernel selector or on-demand codegen?

paola: I rolled the kernel-selection heuristics to canary last night (patch #2357) — it changes preference for fused microkernels on A100 when sequence_length < 256. Might explain different kernel set being chosen.

liam: Also seeing an increase in small-batched requests around the same time — average batcher_window_ms bumped from 8 -> 20ms in a few pods. That could increase latency for first token because batching waits longer and triggers different code paths.

alex.h: Two hypotheses: (1) new kernel preference causes more on-demand kernel loads (kernel_init) + bigger binary size -> init latency; (2) KV cache miss rate spike causing extra retrievetime before decode. We need targeted instrumentation to prove which is dominant.

maya: Agreed. Can we add a split on the token-latency histogram by labels: kernel_name, kernel_selection_reason, kvcache_hit (true/false), batch_size? If we get a small sample of traces we can attribute TTFT to kernel_init vs kvcache fetch.

jordan: I'll add a short-lived trace sampler for requests to /v1/generate capturing: model, kernel_name, kernel_selection_reason, kvcache_hit, batch_size, kernel_load_time_ms, kvcache_fetch_ms. Also add a metric kernel_binary_loads_total and kernel_binary_load_time_seconds histogram.

paola: FYI the canary only changed selection logic, not binary packaging. But selection change could hit a path that loads a fused kernel we haven't warmed yet. We have a warm-cache TTL for kernels but not for fused variants.

liam: Perf bot just fired alert for token_init_surge. perf-bot: Automatic alert: token_kernel_init_count increased by 12x in last 10m on env=prod route=/v1/generate.

perf-bot: Relevant runbook snippets: "If kernel_init_count spikes, check kernel_cache_evictions, recent selector rollouts, and kernel binary size metrics."

alex.h: For quick triage I want two dashboards/queries — one to split p95 TTFT by kvcache_hit and kernel_binary_load (boolean), and a second to show cumulative kernel_binary_load_time by kernel_name over last 2h. Proposed PromQLs: 
```
# TTFT p95 by kv hit (example, adapt names)
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[$__rate_interval])) by (le, kvcache_hit))

# kernel binary load time per kernel
sum(rate(kernel_binary_load_time_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (kernel_name)
```

maya: I'll add a quick temporary chart on the per-route dashboard and add a split by kernel_name. Also will add kernel_selection_reason to the logs we index for the trace sampler.

jordan: Action: enable trace-sampler for 0.5% of requests to /v1/generate, keep for 60m, collect raw spans with kernel tags. I'll also dump a sample span here when available.

paola: For immediate mitigation I can revert the canary at patch #2357 on the nodes serving this route, or we can pin the route to prefer the previous kernel family using per-route override in runtime-config. Which do we prefer?

liam: Revert canary if we're short on time. But pinning per-route is lower blast radius — set kernel_preference: "legacy_fused_prefer=false" for /v1/generate for next 2h.

alex.h: Let's pin the route first (liam + paola), revert canary if metrics don't improve in 30m. Jordan + Maya to produce the kernel vs kvcache split and post sample spans. I'll coordinate postmortem if needed.

perf-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0421 — TTFT spike on /v1/generate. Assigned to oncall-eng-runtime.

paola: Pin applied: runtime-config updated for route /v1/generate -> kernel_preference = legacy_fused_prefer. Rolling config to 3 pods now.

liam: Config rolled to 3/3 pods in the podset, reducing kernel_init_count on those pods. Monitoring...

alex.h: Early signal — p95 TTFT dropped from 700ms -> 240ms on pinned pods. Global p95 still at ~420ms because rollout in progress and kvcache missers still propagating.

maya: Sample span (sanitized):
```
span: request_id=abc123 route=/v1/generate
kvcache_hit=false, kvcache_fetch_ms=150
kernel_selection_reason=selector_v2
kernel_name=fused-gemm-v2
kernel_load_time_ms=410
decode_ms=110
```

jordan: That span basically confirms: kernel_load_time (410ms) + kvcache_fetch (150ms) -> most of TTFT. Two levers: warm fused kernels proactively, and improve kvcache locality or prefetch.

alex.h: Updated action list: 1) Warm fused kernels for models on A100 (ops: liam) 2) Short-term per-route pin (done) 3) Add kernel_binary_load metrics & dashboard (maya) 4) Trace sampler + sample dump (jordan) 5) Investigate kvcache miss correlation with recent eviction policy tweak (paola). Owners assigned.

paola: I'll look at kernel cache eviction/size config and recent kvcache eviction thresholds; will revert changes if correlated.

liam: Ops will add a cron to pre-warm fused kernels for top-10 models in the cluster; will be done within 2h.

alex.h: Thanks everyone. Keep updates here — if we get another regression after unpinning we escalate to rollback. :lock: :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maya: Will follow up with dashboard links and the Prometheus queries once graphs are up.

jordan: Will post 5 sample spans and the query used to pull them in ~20m.

perf-bot: INC-2026-0421 status: mitigation in progress. Monitor metrics for 30m before clearing alert.
